title: When Man Grows Bold in Sin
description: When Man Grows Bold in Sin in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 36, part 3, headed “The wickedness of man, and the majesty of God; or. Practical atheism exposed”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: When man grows bold in sin My heart with-in me cries, "He hath no faith of God with-in, Nor fear be-fore his eyes."

lines: When man grows bold in sin
"He hath no faith of God within,
Till his dark crimes at once reveal'd
His heart is false and foul,
His words are smooth and fair;
Wisdom is banish'd from his soul,
He sets his heart, and hand, and head,
His justice hid behind the cloud
Deep as the sea his judgments lie,
O never let my soul remove

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
